negative_findings.description: Czech-language searches for GoPay partnership press releases returned only help-centre documentation and blog posts; no dedicated 'tiskové zprávy' / press-release section for GoPay was located in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: GoPay appears to communicate partnerships through its blog rather than a formal newsroom; partnership announcements must be reconstructed from blog posts and third-party media.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design for GoPay must target the blog and ČTK wire rather than an expected /press endpoint, otherwise partnership events will be missed.

negative_findings.description: Czech-language searching for ThePay, Barion CZ, Adyen CZ, Stripe CZ and Revolut Business CZ returned mostly third-party integration help pages (webczech, wpjshop, Dativery) rather than the vendors' own Czech-market communications.
negative_findings.result_summary: No CZ-localized newsroom or country page was surfaced for Adyen, Stripe, Barion or Revolut in this pass; Revolut in particular did not appear in softPOS/terminal supplier results for CZ.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The international-entrant leg of the cell is currently evidenced only indirectly. Their CZ presence may have to be tracked via the ČNB/JERRS register, EU passporting notifications and merchant-side integration docs rather than vendor PR.

negative_findings.description: Searches for CZ terminal-vendor case studies (Ingenico, PAX, Verifone, distributors) returned only user manuals, ECR integration FAQs and a US retailer comparison blog — no Czech merchant case-study library.
negative_findings.result_summary: Terminal hardware vendors do not appear to publish CZ-specific case studies publicly; the closest substitutes are bank merchant manuals and ERP integration matrices.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The 'case studies' topic for the terminal estate will have to be served by proxies (public contract register, ERP support matrices, bank manuals) rather than vendor marketing collateral.

negative_findings.description: KB SmartPay and Visa CZ newsroom entry URLs were inferred from brand names and third-party references rather than confirmed by fetching the pages during this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Both are recorded with reduced confidence and access_status 'unverified'; the deterministic liveness pass should resolve their canonical paths.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Two significant actors (KB's acquiring arm and the Visa scheme) would otherwise be under-covered if the guessed URLs fail.

coverage_gaps.description: International PSP entrants into CZ (Adyen, Stripe, Revolut Business, Klarna, PayU, Mollie) are not yet covered by any direct source in this slice; only third-party integration pages evidence their presence.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated pass on ČNB/JERRS passporting entries plus each vendor's country/newsroom pages and their Czech-language merchant docs; add PayU CZ and Klarna CZ explicitly (both appeared in the Shoptet partner marketplace).

coverage_gaps.description: Account-to-account / instant payment rails competing with cards in CZ (CERTIS, okamžité platby, bank-transfer buttons, Shoptet Pay's A2A methods) were not systematically scouted in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a targeted pass on ČNB CERTIS / okamžité platby statistics and on A2A-based CZ gateways, since these directly erode the card acquiring economics this cell tracks.

coverage_gaps.description: No company-registry or financial-statement source was captured for CZ payments entities (justice.cz / obchodní rejstřík, sbírka listin), which would give ownership, group structure and revenue for gateways and terminal vendors.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add or.justice.cz (obchodní rejstřík + sbírka listin) as a systematic source keyed on the actor list produced from SBK membership and ČNB registers.

coverage_gaps.description: Public procurement of terminals and acquiring services (NEN, Věstník veřejných zakázek, TED) was not scouted; these tenders name incumbent suppliers, contract values and renewal dates.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add NEN/VVZ/TED with CPV codes for payment terminals and financial services as a recurring query set.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language coverage of CZ payments was thin in this pass — group-level newsrooms (Global Payments/Worldpay divestiture on Businesswire, Worldline and Mastercard Europe feeds) were touched but not systematically mapped for Czech relevance.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add an en-language pass over group investor-relations and Businesswire/PR Newswire feeds, filtering for 'Czech', 'Czechia', 'CEE' to catch M&A that reshapes the CZ acquiring estate.

brief: The CZ payments-native landscape splits cleanly into four evidence layers. Direct actor sources are strong and mostly open: the three acquirer estates (Global Payments CZ, ČSOB platbakartou.csob.cz, KB SmartPay), the domestic gateways (Comgate, GoPay, ThePay, Pays, Shoptet Pay) and the scheme newsrooms (Mastercard CZ in Czech, Visa CZ). The richest POINTER layer is platform marketplaces and integration documentation — doplnky.shoptet.cz/category/platby and partneri.shoptet.cz effectively enumerate the merchant-facing PSP set, while ERP/ECR help centres (Stormware Pohoda, ABRA Flexi, KASAmax, Payten/Sonet) indirectly expose the terminal estate, acquirer protocols and hardware models nobody publishes on purpose. Authoritative structure comes from the regulator and the industry association: ČNB's JERRS registers define who may legally act as a PSP, and SBK (bankovnikarty.cz) supplies quarterly terminal, contactless and card-accepting-e-shop statistics plus a member list that doubles as an actor map. The main weaknesses are international entrants (Adyen, Stripe, Revolut, Klarna, PayU) which are visible only through third-party integration pages, the absence of any CZ terminal-vendor case-study library, and unscouted corporate-registry and public-procurement layers — all of which are recorded as gaps rather than dead ends.
